quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are normally rectangular. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you usually use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, ride in the left portion of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which portion of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion
The shoulder

questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light. It is not as noticeable as a car's two brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps others see it, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: A motorist driving behind a motorcycle should increase their following distance by a minimum of:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Eight seconds.

questions.explanation: Drivers behind a motorcycle should allow three to four extra seconds of distance. Motorcycles stop faster than cars. Extra space helps both vehicles stop safely in an emergency.

questions.question: When riding at night, a motorcyclist should maintain a minimum following distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. It takes longer to notice when the vehicle stops, and you need more time to slow down.

questions.question: If attempting to brake in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: When leaning in a curve, your tires have less grip than when the motorcycle is upright. If you must brake while turning, brake more gently and smoothly than you would on a straight road.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move into the portion of the lane farthest from the passing vehicle because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The portion of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to experience a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not ride on the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle. This may encourage the driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is the safest way to approach them?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.
Approach at a 45-degree angle.
Approach at a 90-degree angle.
Go at a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad tracks is to go straight in your lane. Turning to approach the tracks at a right angle can be dangerous because it may push you into another lane.

questions.question: During the day, should you use your headlights?

options.text: No, do not use them.
Yes, use high beams.
Yes, use low beams.
Yes, switch between high and low beams.

questions.explanation: Using your high beam headlights during the day helps other drivers see you. Use high beams any time you are not riding directly behind or toward other vehicles.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your reaction time, keep your hands near the clutch and brakes. This is especially helpful when riding through areas with hazards.

questions.question: When braking, how should you apply the brakes?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Apply the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always apply both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What gives you the maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.explanation: Maximum braking power in a straight line comes from applying both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They will likely never need to be replaced.
They develop scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They develop scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic and develop scratches and become brittle over time. Replace them regularly to keep your protection and comfort at their best.
